version.changelog: backlog: stop advertising an unimplemented feature

llm.summary: This VMware policy skill is not malicious, but its documented policy bypasses and fail-open defaults make it worth manual review before relying on it for production safeguards.

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is coherent: shared audit logging, policy checks, and sanitization for VMware skills. However, for a security-control layer wrapping high-impact VMware operations, the artifacts document permissive defaults and bypass modes that weaken the claimed enforcement role.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The skill is clearly marked as a non-user-invocable dependency and says it activates through wrapped VMware tools or audit CLI use. Broad activation across the VMware skill family is disclosed and purpose-aligned.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Installation is a disclosed uv package install for vmware-policy, with no hidden installer steps in the artifact. Static scan and VirusTotal telemetry are clean.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill writes local audit records containing parameters, results, user, agent, and workflow metadata, and it detects agent-related environment variables. This fits audit logging, but retention, minimization, and export-handling guidance are limited.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: It persists a SQLite audit database under ~/.vmware with rotation, hot-loads policy rules from ~/.vmware/rules.yaml, and allows all operations when rules are absent or PyYAML is missing; VMWARE_POLICY_DISABLED=1 bypasses policy checks globally while still logging.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Install only if you understand that audit logging is active but policy enforcement is not protective by default. For production VMware environments, create and test ~/.vmware/rules.yaml, ensure PyYAML is installed, restrict permissions on ~/.vmware and audit exports, and avoid setting VMWARE_POLICY_DISABLED except for tightly controlled troubleshooting.
llm.findings:
[SQP-1] expected: Auto-loading as a dependency is disclosed in SKILL.md and matches the role of a shared decorator and audit/policy layer, so this is not independently suspicious.
[SQP-2] unexpected: The global VMWARE_POLICY_DISABLED=1 bypass is artifact-backed and materially weakens a policy-enforcement layer for high-impact VMware actions.
[SQP-2] expected: Logging parameters, results, user, agent, and workflow metadata is expected for an audit tool, but the artifact gives limited privacy, retention, and minimization controls beyond local storage and rotation.
[SQP-2] expected: JSON audit export is expected functionality, but the CLI reference does not warn that exported audit records may contain sensitive operational metadata.
[SQP-2] unexpected: The setup guide documents fail-open behavior when PyYAML is missing, which is a material concern for a component users may treat as an enforcement control.
[SQP-2] unexpected: The setup guide states that without ~/.vmware/rules.yaml all operations are allowed, creating a permissive default for a policy engine.
